on_the_wire: Bluetooth LE to the Ionic IC-12V40-S9H's own BMS. Two independent reads, both proven from the car 2026-09-08 (D-330): the advertisement's manufacturer data begins with pack millivolts and needs no connection at all; a Read or notification on characteristic FFE1 of service FFE0 returns 7E 01 08, four little-endian uint16 cell counts at about 1.43 mV per count, checksum, 0D
carrier_stage: ESP32-C3 module (XIAO ESP32C3 class) on its own 3.3 V LDO - the Teensy's 250 mA regulator has no headroom for a BLE scan (D-273): UART TX / RX to the Teensy on Serial2, EN and BOOT to two GPIOs so the Teensy can reset and reflash it, antenna end overhanging the board edge with a 5 mm keep-out toward an RF-transparent enclosure wall
teensy_pin: Serial2: RX 7 (from the radio's TX) / TX 8; EN 34, BOOT 35
calibration: None on this board - the BMS calibrates itself and the ICU republishes. Cross-check at bring-up: the four cell counts summed must agree with the advertised pack millivolts, which is how the 1.43 mV scale was confirmed
can: 0x220 out, 2 Hz, 8 bytes, little-endian: bytes 0-1 pack mV u16 (advertisement) · bytes 2-3 cell 1 mV u16 · 4-5 cell 2 mV · 6 flags. 0x221 out, 2 Hz: bytes 0-1 cell 3 mV · 2-3 cell 4 mV · 4-5 spread mV u16 · 6 flags. Flags bit 0 advertisement fresh (under 10 s) · bit 1 GATT connected · bit 2 cell frame fresh · bit 3 checksum failed. Pack current, state of charge and temperature have NO source and are not published - the type-01 frame does not carry them (D-330, W-330b)
note: Runs only while the ICU does - the logic rail is O10, accessory - so the overnight story is read at key-on from the source's own counters. Scan always; connect to FFE1 only when cell detail is wanted, one connection at a time, and never write. FFE7 and anything labelled DFU are never touched: that is the firmware-update path on the BMS that runs the car's power. Bring-up on a dev board first (P116). A field with no source is left undefined rather than published as zero - a zero on the bus is a number and someone will believe it
